messages.subject: Read.cross and RIL population
messages.subject_clean: Read.cross and RIL population
messages.body_plain:
Hi Karl,

I am trying to analyze several populations of RIL maize using ScanOne and MQMScan, but I am unsure as how to Load the data, one option would be:

 POP02A<-read.cross("csv",file="POP02.csv", genotypes=c("0","2"), na.strings="NaN", allele=c("A","B"),  crosstype="riself")

but this option drops the genotypes  0.5,1.0 and 1.5 in my data (My data set has no missing information), and lowers the LOD scores when using Scanone (ascompared to when I use the same formula including "1" as HZ)

In you Q&A section of the website you recommend uploading as a backcross and then expanding it:

POP02A<-read.cross("csv",file="POP02.csv", genotypes=c("0","2"), na.strings="NaN", allele=c("A","B"))
POP02A<- convert2riself(POP02A)

What would you recommend? what would be best for single and MQM ?

Thank you very much,

Bryan

messages.subject_clean: The unique identifier for the genotypes, "Genotype", cannot be found in the object
messages.body_plain:
Hello folks,

Has anyone ran into this problem. I can read the .csv file and read my cross data but it will not make or read unique identifiers for the genotypes.

This causes problems later on, because I cannot use any functions including profileGen(), statGen(), etc.

I tried assigning unique identifiers by using
row.names(hap$geno$`1`$data) <- hap$pheno$ï..Genotype

Where:
hap = is the name of the cross object
Genotype in hap$pheno = the unique identifier for my genotype

'1' = All the genotype data in one linkage group (no ordering of markers have been done)

Please let me know if you know the solution to this problem, thank you.

Kind Regards,

Miguel

messages.body_plain:
R/qtl can't deal with phased F2 data, unless you were going to try to treat it as a phase-known 4-way cross, in which case the coding is much more complicated.

I'd switch the coding to AA:AB:BB, and on the X chromosome males AA:BB and females AB:BB, and with a phenotype column pgm==1.

karl

messages.subject: NAs in RF matrix with partially missing 4-way markers
messages.subject_clean: NAs in RF matrix with partially missing 4-way markers
messages.body_plain:
Hi Karl et al.
I'm working with a genetic map construction tool that requires a complete recombination fraction matrix - that is, no NAs in the upper triangle of `pull.rf(cross, what = "rf")`. However, when using a 4-way cross where some markers have partial missing genotypes, I get some NAs in the rf matrix. These NAs are distributed among markers with both high and low recombination fractions, so just setting them as a constant (e.g. 0.5) does not work.

I don't get NA's but do get a warning about no convergence with partial missing data in the F2.

I'm sure that this issue must arise when marker pairs share the partial missing genotype within an individual. Therefore it would be impossible to infer the exact number of recombinants. I'm hoping it would be a simple fix to ignore these NAs in est_rf_4way.

Any help is appreciated.
Thanks,
John

Here is a reproducible example:

```{r}
#####
# F2 example
set.seed(42)
map = sim.map(sex.sp = F)
set.seed(42)
cross = sim.cross(map = map, map.function = "kosambi", partial.missing.prob = .1, type = "f2")
cross<-est.rf(cross) # note no convergence
plot.rf(cross)

rf = pull.rf(cross, what = "rf")
sum(is.na <http://is.na>(rf[upper.tri(rf)])) # no NAs

#####
# 4way example
set.seed(42)
map = sim.map(sex.sp = T)
set.seed(42)
cross = sim.cross(map = map, map.function = "kosambi", partial.missing.prob = .1, type = "4way")
cross<-est.rf(cross)
plot.rf(cross)

rf = pull.rf(cross, what = "rf")
sum(is.na <http://is.na>(rf[upper.tri(rf)]))
```

messages.body_plain:
There’s no way around these NAs. In a phase-known 4-way cross there are some possible marker pairs for which you have no information about linkage, for example if one marker is only informative in one parent and the other marker is only informative in the other parent.

karl
